The mathematics graduate program at Dartmouth College is a
small, selective program that serves students who wish to
complete a PhD in pure or applied mathematics. The program is
structured to serve both those who envision a career involving
research and teaching as well as those who wish to continue
their research in industry. It is a five-year program in which
students are enrolled in each of the Summer, Fall, Winter, and
Spring terms. Students who are admitted to the PhD program are
offered support through a Dartmouth Fellowship or other grant
for up to five years provided they continue to make satisfactory
progress towards their degree.
Read the PhD
requirements and timeline which includes the steps towards
completing your degree.
If you are considering applying to the graduate program here,
we advise you to review the research interests of our faculty to
make sure there are a few areas of interest to you. Make sure
to solidify your understanding of the advanced undergraduate
courses available for your major, as this will ease your entry
into graduate work.
Areas which students have recently chosen for their dissertation research include algebraic number theory, algebraic geometry, algebraic topology, arithmetic geometry, combinatorics, complex networks/systems, data science, evolutionary game theory, functional analysis, knot theory, logic, machine learning, mathematical biology, numerical analysis, Riemannian geometry, set theory, and signal processing. Review
their thesis abstracts
and advisor and job
information.
For additional information about our program, please visit
our Graduate Student Info page
and our FAQ for Applicants page.
For information about the Dartmouth graduate student community, including housing, social events, and further support, visit the Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies website.
You may also contact our department information manager by email
at mits.kobayashi@dartmouth.edu.
Application Requirements
Application deadline: December 15, 2026.
All application materials must be received by the deadline in order to receive full consideration.
Apply online through the Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies. Application link: https://apply.gs.dartmouth.edu/apply
For all official application requirements and further application information and FAQ pages, see the Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies' site for the Mathematics PhD program:
https://graduate.dartmouth.edu/academics/programs/mathematics
Three letters of recommendation.
Both the GRE general exam and the GRE math subject exam are optional. If you feel that your GRE math subject exam score contributes positively to your application, then we encourage you to submit it, and unofficial scores will be provisionally accepted.
Official English language proficiency test scores are required for students for whom English is not their first language. This requirement can be waived for students who study for four years at a US college or university and graduate with a bachelor’s degree.
For information on the Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies' application fee waiver program:
https://graduate.dartmouth.edu/admissions-financial-aid/applying-dartmouth/fee-waiver-criteria
Official transcripts (and GRE scores, if you submit them) will be required if you are offered admission to the program and accept the offer. On the application, you be required to upload unofficial transcripts.
Financial Information
The PhD program in Mathematics is fully funded. For details, see the Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies's site on funding:
https://graduate.dartmouth.edu/admissions-financial-aid/funding
